meta.title: Hoshizora · Space data analytics
meta.description: Launches, near-Earth asteroids and space weather from agencies worldwide, gathered into one clean dataset where every number traces back to its source.

dataLink.wakingDetail: The data service rests when nobody is visiting. It usually wakes within a minute.
dataLink.offlineDetail: Still retrying every 30 seconds. Everything else on the page keeps working.
dataLink.failed: This data could not be loaded.
dataLink.failedDetail: The data service answered with an error. Try again, or come back in a few minutes.

footer.data: Data from Launch Library 2 (The Space Devs), CelesTrak, NASA/JPL CNEOS, NOAA SWPC and the NASA Exoplanet Archive.
footer.trace: Every number links back to the records behind it.

home.title: Every number has a source.
home.lede: Hoshizora gathers launch, orbit, asteroid and space-weather data from agencies around the world and turns it into facts you can trace back to the original records.

facts.title: Top facts
facts.lede: The most unusual numbers in the data right now, each one computed from source records.

launches.title: Launches
launches.lede: Every orbital launch attempt on record: who flies, how often, and how often it works.

nearEarth.title: Near-Earth objects
nearEarth.lede: Asteroids and comets passing close to Earth, how big they might be, and the few with a tiny chance of impact.

sun.title: The Sun and space weather
sun.lede: Solar flares, the solar wind and the geomagnetic storms that light up the aurora.

exoplanets.title: Exoplanets
exoplanets.lede: Planets around other stars: how they were found, how big they are, and how close the nearest ones lie.

agencies.title: Agencies
agencies.lede: The space agencies, companies and armed forces behind the world's launches.

sources.title: Sources and credits
sources.lede: Where every number comes from, under which license, and how fresh it is.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: Nothing is orbiting at this address.

crash.title: Something went wrong on this page.
crash.body: The rest of Hoshizora is fine. Reload the page, or head back home.

cadence.title: Launches per year by national program
cadence.lede: Every orbital launch attempt since 1957, grouped by the national program behind it.
cadence.description: Launch attempts per year for the six busiest programs, with the world total as a gray line. Complete years only.

success.title: How often launches succeed
success.lede: Share of completed launches that reached orbit, over all time and over each program's last 20 launches.
success.description: Bars show the all-time success rate; the marker shows the rate over the last 20 launches.

pads.title: Busiest launch pads
pads.lede: Pads ranked by the launch attempts on record.
pads.description: Launch attempts from the ten busiest pads.

reusability.title: Flying the same booster again
reusability.lede: Launches whose first stage had flown before, and how often boosters landed, year by year.
reusability.description: Launches with a recorded first stage per year, split by whether the booster was new or had flown before. The line shows the share of landing attempts that succeeded. Complete years only.

boosters.title: Most flown boosters
boosters.lede: Individual first stages ranked by how many times they have flown.
boosters.description: Flights of the ten most flown first stages. Stages whose serial was never published are left out.

monthly.title: Close approaches per month
monthly.lede: Asteroids and comets passing within 0.05 au (about 19.5 Earth–Moon distances) of Earth, from a year ago to a year ahead.
monthly.description: Approaches per month; the amber part of each bar came closer than the Moon. Future months, drawn fainter, are predictions.

sizeDistance.title: Size and distance, next 60 days
sizeDistance.lede: Each dot is one predicted flyby. Sizes come from brightness and an assumed reflectivity, so each is a range.
sizeDistance.description: Miss distance in Earth–Moon distances (left is closer) against the estimated diameter in meters, both on log scales. The line marks the Moon's distance.

sentry.title: Impact risk watch list
sentry.lede: NASA's Sentry system lists objects whose orbits cannot yet rule out an impact within about 100 years. Almost all are removed as new observations arrive.
sentry.palermoNote: Palermo scale: below −2 means no concern; 0 means as risky as the background chance of an unknown impact.

kp.title: Geomagnetic activity, past 7 days
kp.lede: Planetary Kp every three hours. Kp 5 or more is a geomagnetic storm (NOAA G1 and above).
kp.description: Kp per three-hour interval; amber bars reached storm level.

flares.title: Solar flares, past 7 days
flares.lede: X-ray flares seen by the GOES satellites. Each class is ten times stronger than the one before: A, B, C, M, X.
flares.description: Peak X-ray flux of each flare over time, on a log scale.

wind.title: Solar wind, past 7 days
wind.lede: Measured about 1.5 million km upstream of Earth. Fast wind and a southward field (negative Bz) feed geomagnetic storms.
wind.bzDescription: Hourly mean north–south magnetic field; negative values point south.

aurora.title: Where the aurora may be visible
aurora.lede: NOAA's OVATION model forecasts the chance of seeing aurora about 30 to 90 minutes ahead. Each dot is one 1° cell; brighter means likelier.
aurora.history: Highest chance per forecast, past 48 hours
aurora.historyDescription: Each hemisphere's highest probability of visible aurora in each hourly forecast.
aurora.mapLabel: Polar map of aurora probability, {{hemisphere}}, centered on the pole with rings every 10° of latitude.

profile.cadenceDescription: Launch attempts per year as the launch provider.

sources.fontsLede: Both typefaces are used under the SIL Open Font License.
sources.gapsBody: Roscosmos and CNSA offer no general-purpose public launch or mission APIs, and the community SpaceX API is no longer updated. Their launches and objects come from Launch Library 2 and CelesTrak.

discoveries.title: Discoveries per year
discoveries.lede: Every confirmed exoplanet by the year it was announced and the method that found it.
discoveries.description: Confirmed planets per discovery year, split by the four most productive methods. Complete years only.

sizeOrbit.title: Sizes and orbits
sizeOrbit.lede: Transiting planets on a grid of orbital period and radius. Larger circles hold more planets.
sizeOrbit.description: Both axes are logarithmic. Only transiting planets are shown, because a transit measures a planet's radius directly; other methods mostly estimate it. Earth and Jupiter are marked for scale.

nearest.title: The nearest known exoplanets
nearest.lede: The ten nearest known exoplanets, nearest first.
nearest.note: Radii of planets that were not seen transiting are estimated from their mass. Planets whose confirmation has been questioned are left out.

exoplanets.acknowledgment: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
